requirement_text.REQ-152: RESTATEMENT OF LUA-14. LUA-14 (Time Source, MUST) reads: "platform.now() MUST return the platform's authoritative time as ISO 8601 UTC. Lua's os.time MUST NOT be available." Lua.new/1's documented default sandbox denies 6 of 11 os functions (execute, exit, getenv, remove, rename, tmpname). It does NOT deny os.clock, os.date, os.difftime, os.setlocale, os.time. os.time is therefore reachable unless denied explicitly. This requirement closes that gap for the 4 ambient time functions (os.time, os.date, os.clock, os.difftime) -- going BEYOND LUA-14's literal wording (which names only os.time) as a deliberate extension of intent (os.date/os.clock/os.difftime are also ambient time sources). os.setlocale is not a time source and falls to REQ-151's general enumeration. THE :sandboxed TRAP: constructing the sandbox via `sandboxed: [[:os, :time]]` would un-deny all 27 defaults including os.execute and load -- whichever mechanism is used, a test must assert default denials still hold afterward. Scope: 1. Extend REQ-151's sandbox construction (lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex) so os.time, os.date, os.clock, os.difftime are all unreachable from a script, without un-denying any default. 2. Implement platform.now() returning Letflow's authoritative time as an ISO 8601 UTC string. Per R-Co's capability matrix, now is UNGATED BY DESIGN -- a pure time read with no state reach, a positive design statement not an omission; record this in the moduledoc so REQ-157's capability work does not later add a gate to it by symmetry. 3. The time source must be injectable so tests can assert an exact value rather than a plausible-looking one -- do not read the system clock directly at the call site. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no other platform.* function (REQ-157, REQ-159, REQ-160). GATE: SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate -- this modifies the sandbox boundary.

task.description: CODE-DESIGNER (WF-02 Step 1) for REQ-152. Write lib/letflow/design/req152-lua-time-denial.md covering the sandbox extension and platform.now() implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Design shows exactly how os.time, os.date, os.clock, os.difftime become unreachable from a script without un-denying any Lua.new/1 default (name the mechanism, e.g. explicit sandbox table entries vs the :sandboxed trap, and explain why the chosen mechanism avoids the trap)

Design specifies platform.now/0's public signature, its ISO 8601 UTC string return type, and how the time source is injected for testability (e.g. a behaviour/callback module, application env, or explicit arg) rather than reading the system clock directly at the call site
Design states platform.now is ungated by design per R-Co's capability matrix and that this is a positive design statement, so future capability work (REQ-157) must not add a gate to it

Design covers all 7 acceptance criteria listed in docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-152 entry (read it directly for the full test-level acceptance criteria list -- os.time/date/clock/difftime nil-or-raise test, default-denial-still-holds test, remaining os functions nil-or-raise test, platform.now DateTime-parseable test, injectable-exact-timestamp test, moduledoc content, mix test/compile passing)
No implementation code (.ex bodies) -- signatures and type shapes only
Open questions listed explicitly if any exist, not silently resolved

result.summary: Design extends REQ-151's Sandbox.new/1 deny-set from 28 to 33 entries (adds os.time, os.date, os.clock, os.difftime, and a gap-closure entry for os.setlocale which REQ-151's implementation omitted despite its own description claiming coverage). Adds new Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform module: now/0 (ISO 8601 UTC string), a TimeSource behaviour resolved via application env (not a direct clock read) for exact-value test injection, and install/1 wiring platform.now into the Lua VM via Lua.set!/3, called from Sandbox.new/1's construction pipeline. platform.now is documented as ungated by design, binding on REQ-157. All 8 REQ-152 acceptance criteria mapped to concrete design elements (design doc section 6). Open questions: OQ-1 (os.setlocale gap, disposition made explicit), OQ-2 (os.time_ms/time_us left out of scope), OQ-3 (config file location for app-env default), OQ-4 (assumes REQ-151/148 mix.exs dependency question already resolved).
